TRENT UNIVERSITY ARCHIVES — CAMPING ACCESSIONS SWEPT FOR KANAWANA, OTOREKE, QUEBEC, YMCA, MONTREAL
===================================================================================================
Swept 2026-09-06. Every accession fetched RAW from archives.trentu.ca and searched; nothing here is a
summarizer's reading. The records themselves are not digitized — these are finding aids.

ACCESSIONS SWEPT: 72-007 (OCA original), 78-006, 82-009, 84-019, 85-011, 86-018, 88-006, 89-015,
92-005, 93-021, 82-016 (Perry), 80-022 (Northway), 83-002 (CCA sound tapes), 85-013 (QCA), 78-004 (CCA).

THE HITS THAT NAME KANAWANA OR MONTREAL
---------------------------------------
78-006, SERIES F, BOX 24, FOLDER 25 — "Agency Camps 'Y' camps: - Wanakita, Wa-sa-ah-bun, Tapatoo,
    Tapawingo, Pinecrest, Camp Stephens and KANAWANA; 'Church' camps: De LaSalle, Simpresca,
    Quin-mo-lac, Moorelands - Kawagama and Kingswood; YMCA day and resident camp brochure;
    Haliburton Scout Reserve - Staff policy book". Series F is CAMP LITERATURE AND BROCHURES
    (CIRCA 1970'S). **A Kanawana brochure of the 1970s, in an Ontario fonds.**

84-019, BOX 1, FOLDER 10 — "YMCA - Montreal". A folder with that title and no further description.

THE QUEBEC ASSOCIATION MATERIAL
-------------------------------
78-006, SERIES D, BOX 21:
    F9  Quebec Camping Association, 1977: Historical Summary of QCA; 40th (1977) Conference
        brochures, programmes, literature; Newsletter, Feb. 1977
    F10 Quebec Camping Association, 1966-1975: Correspondence with OCA; Literature and some Camp
        Brochures; QCA Reports; 1970 Standards; QCA Annual Report, 1966; Proposed Constitution;
        Conference literature, 1966; "Plein Air" Scout Booklet
    F11 **Quebec Camping Association MINIMUM STANDARDS, 1970**; Program outlines; By-laws
    F12 **Quebec Camping Association DIRECTORIES, 1967, 1969-1973**; Conference brochures, 1970
88-006, BOX 2:
    F41 Quebec Camping Association (English Section) — minutes, reports, some correspondence, 1972-1977
    F42 Quebec Camping Association (English Section) — correspondence, minutes, reports,
        constitution, 1978-1979
    F20 French Language Conference — Quebec, 1976        F22 Oral History project, 1976-1977
85-013 (the QCA's own fonds):
    Box 1 F1  Camp visitation reports and related correspondence, 1962-1968   [p_339]
    Box 1 F21 Q.C.A. Standards, correspondence, 1953-1973                      [p_346]
    Box 2 F22 Q.C.A. Centennial Commission                                     [p_337]
92-005, SERIES D: F19 "CCA - Correspondence 1968-1975: Correspondence and memos between OCA and CCA,
    QUEBEC CAMPING ASSOCIATION and CCA; report of the task force studying development of the CCA,
    1970; CCA mailing list 1968"; F25 QCA Inc. letterhead. Box 1 F14 is camp brochures by province,
    "Alberta Manitoba New Brunswick QUEBEC Saskatchewan".

THE INTERVIEW MATERIAL, WHICH IS BETTER THAN THE TAPES
------------------------------------------------------
83-002 — Canadian Camping Association fonds : Sound Tape Recordings. Item-level aid. ONE Quebec
    item: 83-002/011/008, MARJORIE BOOTH, interviewed by ELEANOR KAY, 12 November 1991,
    "Involvement with New Brunswick and Quebec Camping Associations. Involvement as Executive
    Director of Canadian Camping Association." Cassette, worksheet, two colour photographs.
84-019, BOX 2, FOLDER 4 — **"Transcripts of some interview tapes previously recorded"**: Omer
    Stringer · Stephen Lewis · Jean Foster · Penny Miall · Tony Fry · Camp Philosophy (CCA meeting,
    1975) · Pat Scollard · Recruiting and Public Relations (CCA Directors Conference, 1975) ·
    Budget and Financial Leadership (CCA Directors Conference, 1975) … **TRANSCRIPTS ARE READABLE
    WHERE TAPES ARE NOT**, and this folder was not known to this project.

THE CENTENARY JOURNEY (p_337)
-----------------------------
72-007, BOX 6 FOLDERS 12-19 and BOX 7 FOLDERS 1-4 at least. TRIP LOGS named in three: F12
    "personnel data sheets, TRIP LOGS, area histories and trip reports"; F13 "personnel lists,
    correspondence, TRIP LOGS"; F15 "routes, schedules, LOGS, etc." Also F17 photographs and
    articles on Quetico and the Peterborough canoe; F19 historical essays on canoe routes, with a
    ROLLED MAP OF THE CENTENARY ROUTE in the Map Collection.

OTHER ITEMS WORTH A LINE
------------------------
78-006, SERIES C, BOX 16 F15-17 and BOX 17 F1-5 — OCA Standards Committee, 1965-1966, COMPLETED
    VISITATION RECORDS FOR CAMPS, filed alphabetically: F17 is "F-K", Box 17 F1 is "K". These are
    the ONTARIO association's visits, so a Quebec camp is not expected; recorded because the shape
    is exactly what p_339 wants from the Quebec side.
78-006, SERIES H, BOX 25 — papers by Mary L. Northway including **"Report of a trip to Twenty-Eight
    Camps in Ontario and QUEBEC", 1940, with Miss Marion Gibson.**
92-005 — "Camp Sights: Desirable Practices for Canadian YMCA Camps", 1965.
72-007, BOX 9 F1 — "'Agency Liaison' material, FROM THE QUEBEC SECTION, Canadian Camping
    Association — correspondence, papers, 1960-1962".

CLEAN NULLS
-----------
80-022 (M. L. Northway fonds): household records, family genealogy tapes, property records, her
    OCA/CCA participation, winding-up of the Northway Company. No Kanawana, Otoreke, Quebec, YMCA
    or Montreal in the description.
85-011, 86-018, 89-015, 93-021, 82-016: Ontario camps and OCA business; no Kanawana, no Otoreke,
    no Montreal. 86-018 and 89-015 carry long alphabetical member-camp runs — all Ontario.
